answer.rationale: p99 latency spike during settlement peak with compliance-mandated security patch rules out rollback. Memory_b3 shows that provisioning headroom before peak load absorption was effective. With writes heavy at daily peak, adding capacity is the safest single intervention that preserves both the security patch and write durability. Memory_b2 documents that regional failover has worked well historically, but failover does not increase write capacity—it redistributes load. Adding capacity directly addresses the root cause (saturation during peak writes) and has precedent for working in similar conditions. Circuit breaker would shed writes, violating the primary objective. Read replicas do not help the write path. One verification confirms headroom strategy is sound for this exact scenario.
